subject: Audit: intermittent checkout latency spike — evidence & remedial ask
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@clearpathretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unusual checkout latency spike (Mar 27) — need evidence for audit

Hi Hannah,

Heads up — during our nightly peak window yesterday (Mar 27) we observed a spike in checkout latency and a small increase in transaction failures. Our internal monitoring shows a 95th percentile response time jump from ~220ms to ~1.8s between 22:45 and 23:20 UTC, and ~0.8% of requests returned 500/502. This impacted ~42 orders.

We have an upcoming compliance audit next Friday and our auditors are asking for vendor confirmation of the service window plus any remediation/credit plans. Please confirm whether Redwood has an observable service degradation or routing fallback during that window and whether this qualifies for SLA remedy under our contract.

I've attached our merchant-side traces and a screenshot of the errors. If you need any additional traces or the billing contact, reply here or loop ops@clearpathretail.com. We're happy to coordinate a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
— Sara
Sara Kim
Head of Site Reliability
ClearPath Retail
attachments: merchant-traces-20290327.csv, screenshot-checkout-errors.png
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@clearpathretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual checkout latency spike (Mar 27) — need evidence for audit

Sara — thanks for the data and the heads up. We take audit timelines seriously; we'll prioritize this.

Quick next steps from our side:
- I'll open an internal evidence pull and ask infra to package request-level traces, autoscaler events, and routing logs for 22:30–23:40 UTC.
- Ben (cc) will do a first-pass classification (full outage vs degraded/latency burst) and confirm potential credit eligibility under the SLA.
- Please confirm the billing contact and whether you want the postmortem redacted for public release or strictly for auditors.

Can you also send any client-side request IDs for a couple of impacted orders (order ids are fine) — that will speed cross-correlation.

Propose a short sync tomorrow at 11:00am PT if that works for you.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual checkout latency spike (Mar 27) — need evidence for audit

Folks — initial findings from the evidence pull (raw artifacts attached):
- raw-trace-shard-7.log: shows a short period where the routing controller moved a subset of checkout traffic to a fallback model variant between 22:47:04–22:58:10 UTC. The fallback increased model latency (95p) due to longer warmup and a temporary KV cache miss pattern.
- gpu-metrics-03-27.json: node-level GPU queue depth spiked on pool-3 during the same window; autoscaler triggered scale-up but pods started 18–23s after the trigger due to coldstart delays.

Classification suggestion: degraded_throughput/latency_burst rather than a full service outage. Under our standard hosted SLA, eligibility for a credit requires a sustained outage or error-rate threshold breach on the ingress tier. The 0.8% error rate and the ~33-minute elevated latency window mean this is borderline — I'd recommend we offer a pro-rated credit as a goodwill/compliance gesture given the audit timeline.

Suggested immediate actions:
- Produce a timeboxed evidence packet: routing events, autoscaler triggers, and request-level traces for the impacted orders (I pulled the traces for the order ids Sara provided).
- Draft a short postmortem focused on root cause (routing fallback + slow coldstart) and mitigations (cache priming, faster pool warmup).
- Offer a one-time pro-rata credit (proposed: 8% for the 33-minute window) while we complete the RCA.

Link to internal draft: https://drive.redwood.internal/rca/CLEARPATH-20290327-draft (view-only for the team).

Attachments: raw-trace-shard-7.log, gpu-metrics-03-27.json

— Ben
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@clearpathretail.com>, ops@clearpathretail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 31 Mar 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unusual checkout latency spike (Mar 27) — evidence & next steps

Sara — thanks for your patience and for sending the order ids. Our initial pass confirms a routing fallback and an elevated 95p latency window between 22:47–23:20 UTC on Mar 27. Ben attached the raw traces and node metrics; we'll finalize the full evidence packet by EOD Tue (Apr 2) and a concise postmortem by Fri Apr 5 so you have it before the audit.

Regarding credits: while this looks like a latency burst rather than a platform-wide outage, given your audit we will classify this as a pro-rata SLA remedy and issue an 8% credit applied to the Apr invoice for impacted usage. If your billing contact is different than ops@clearpathretail.com, please share the correct address so we can route the credit.

Mitigations we're committing to now:
- Cache priming for checkout model variants in the affected pool during high-traffic windows.
- Reduce coldstart latency by pre-warming an additional standby instance in pool-3 for your tenant.
- Add a monitoring alert to flag similar routing fallbacks and page on-call for immediate investigation.

If you'd like a short 20-minute review of the evidence with our SREs before the audit, we can schedule that tomorrow 11:00am PT or Mon 9:00am PT.

Appreciate the flag — we'll keep this narrow and fast.

Best,
— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
